title: Trimodal ground, hover and fixed-wing UAV
description: A modular UAV combines ground motion, hovering and fixed-wing forward flight.
introduction: Different parts of a mission call for different forms of movement. This modular platform combines ground locomotion, hovering and fixed-wing forward flight so that vehicle configuration can follow the task.

problem.heading: One flight mode cannot serve every task equally well.
paragraphs: Hovering is useful for precise observation and manoeuvring, while forward flight offers a different way to cover distance. Ground locomotion can exploit surface support when the robot does not need to remain airborne.
Combining these modes creates a design and integration challenge: the physical platform and onboard control must support several operating configurations without treating each as a separate robot.

approach.heading: Combine three locomotion modes in one platform.
paragraphs: The vehicle integrates ground motion, quadrotor-style hovering and fixed-wing forward flight in a modular platform. ArduPilot integration connects the design with practical onboard operation.

The published work includes wind-tunnel and field evaluation. The project brings together the mechanical configuration, control integration and operating-mode transitions rather than relying only on a design concept.

steps.title: Move on the ground
steps.text: Use supported locomotion where a suitable surface is available.

steps.title: Hover and manoeuvre
steps.text: Use multicopter operation for low-speed positioning.

steps.title: Fly forward
steps.text: Use the winged configuration for forward flight.

evidence.label: Field flight evaluation
evidence.text: The supplied field-test video shows the physical trimodal UAV operating in its flight configurations, with operating-mode annotations.

evidence.label: Ground operation and transitions
evidence.text: A separate field recording demonstrates ground navigation and transitions. It complements the flight tests rather than serving as a simulation of them.

evidence.label: Range and endurance
evidence.text: The paper’s range estimates are configuration-specific and derived from measured power and an assumed battery capacity. Range and endurance are different quantities; no universal mission multiplier is claimed here.
